title: FSANZ energy statement for packaged alcoholic beverages

versions.notes: Initial rules, transcribed from Build Brief 01 sections 2, 7 and 8. The primary sources were NOT re-read: www.foodstandards.gov.au, www.wineaustralia.com and www.legislation.gov.au were blocked by the network policy of the session-1 build environment, so every regulatory verified_at is null. The two studio rules sourced only from the brief (min_rule_weight_pt, servings_decimal_places) are verified against Build Brief 01. Search-engine excerpts retrieved on 2026-09-27 are consistent with the compliance date, the 0.5% ABV threshold, the bordered tabular format and the averages requirement, but they are not a substitute for reading the sources.

Verified against the Code amendment (Gazette No. FSC 181, Amendment No. 241), the FSANZ guidance of February 2026 and the Wine Australia fact sheet v1.2, all supplied by Komms-Haus; each source records the SHA-256 of the copy read. Changes: standard drinks move into the serving-size line, as the prescribed format sets out ('Serving size: 60 mL (1 standard drink)'), so the standard_drinks_per_serving label is removed and standard_drinks_words added; standard_drinks_trim_trailing_zero follows the guidance example; standardised_alcoholic_beverages added, because they need the statement at any ABV; exemptions reworded to the Code; existing_duties no longer lists alcohol content, which none of the sources mentions; min_type_size confirmed as none. Still unverified: ethanol_density_g_per_ml and kj_per_cal, which none of the three sources states.

Komms-Haus accepted ethanol_density_g_per_ml (0.789 g/mL, ethanol at 20 °C) and kj_per_cal (4.184 kJ per kilocalorie) as physical constants on 30 September 2026. Neither is stated in the Code amendment, the FSANZ guidance or the Wine Australia fact sheet. Every rule is now verified.

gazettal_date.locator: Gazette No. FSC 181 cover; P1059 Variation clause 3 (commences on gazettal); fact sheet p. 1

compliance_date.locator: P1059 Variation clause 4(4) (transition period ends 36 months after commencement); guidance p. 6; fact sheet p. 2
compliance_date.notes: Products packaged and labelled on or after this date must carry the statement. Products packaged and labelled before it may still be sold afterwards (clause 4(3)).

min_abv_percent.locator: Standard 2.7.1—2, definition of prescribed beverage, paragraph (b); guidance p. 1
min_abv_percent.notes: Inclusive: beverages containing no less than 0.5% alcohol by volume. Standardised alcoholic beverages are covered at any ABV; see standardised_alcoholic_beverages.

standardised_alcoholic_beverages.locator: Standard 2.7.1—2, definition of prescribed beverage, paragraph (a); guidance p. 1; fact sheet p. 4
standardised_alcoholic_beverages.notes: These need the statement at any ABV, including versions under 0.5% ABV (guidance p. 1).

value.description: The beverage has a nutrition information panel required by Standard 1.2.8, or a voluntary one that complies with section 2.7.1—4E.
The beverage is for sale in a small package: a package with a surface area of less than 100 cm².
The food is not required to bear a label.

exemptions.notes: The not-required-to-bear-a-label exemption comes from the guidance (p. 1). It follows from the labelling provisions in Standard 1.2.1, not from section 2.7.1—4A.

title_text.locator: Standard 2.7.1—4B(3); guidance p. 2; fact sheet p. 2

table_with_borders.locator: Standard 2.7.1—4B(3) (prescribed format); fact sheet p. 2 ('prescribed tabular format with borders')
table_with_borders.notes: The prescribed format is a bordered box: the heading centred above the servings and serving size lines, a rule, the column headings, a rule, then the Energy row. There is no rule under the heading and none between columns. packages/panel/src/layout.ts follows this arrangement.

labels.notes: Wording of the prescribed format. {package} is replaced by the package word. Standard drinks are not a separate line: they follow the serving size in brackets, e.g. 'Serving size: 60 mL (1 standard drink)'.

standard_drinks_words.locator: Standard 2.7.1—4B(3) ('([insert number] standard drinks)'); guidance p. 2 example ('(1 standard drink)')

column_headings.locator: Standard 2.7.1—4B(3) and 2.7.1—4C(1); guidance p. 2; fact sheet p. 5
column_headings.notes: The prescribed headings are 'Quantity per serving' and 'Quantity per 100 mL', and section 2.7.1—4C(1) requires the statement to indicate clearly that the quantities are averages. These headings follow the guidance example, which does that in the column headings.

energy_units.notes: Per serving and per 100 mL, in kJ or in both kJ and kilocalories, set out as 'kJ (Cal)'.

max_significant_figures.notes: A ceiling. Section 2.7.1—4C(4) also allows an average energy content under 40 kJ to be expressed as 'LESS THAN 40 kJ'; the generator does not offer that yet.

standard_drinks_decimal_places.notes: Accurate to the first decimal place.

standard_drinks_trim_trailing_zero.locator: guidance p. 2, example ('Serving size: 60 mL (1 standard drink)')
standard_drinks_trim_trailing_zero.notes: Whole numbers are shown without '.0', as in the guidance example. The Code requires accuracy to the first decimal place (2.7.1—4B(2)); set false to always show one decimal place, e.g. '1.0 standard drinks'.

package_word.notes: 'package' may be replaced by 'can', 'bottle' or any other word or words that accurately describe the package. Cask and keg are studio presets from Build Brief 01.

value: the approximate number of standard drinks in the package
existing_duties.locator: Standard 2.7.1—4(1A); guidance p. 2, Note 2; fact sheet pp. 7–8
existing_duties.notes: The separate statement of standard drinks in the package must still appear elsewhere on the label, and must not appear inside the energy statement (2.7.1—4(1A)). Shown to the user as a reminder, never inside the panel. Build Brief 01 also listed alcohol content; none of these sources mentions it, so it is not included.

standard_drink_ethanol_g.locator: fact sheet pp. 2 and 5, quoting the Code's definition of standard drink ('10 grams of ethanol when measured at 20°C')

ethanol_density_g_per_ml.notes: Density of ethanol at 20 °C, the temperature at which the Code measures standard drinks (see standard_drink_ethanol_g). Accepted by Komms-Haus as a physical constant; none of the regulatory sources on file states it.

kj_per_cal.notes: Cal = kJ / 4.184: one kilocalorie is 4.184 kJ. Accepted by Komms-Haus as a physical constant; none of the regulatory sources on file states it.

servings_decimal_places.locator: Build Brief 01 section 7; fact sheet p. 2 ('number of servings per package ..., accurate to one decimal place')
servings_decimal_places.notes: Servings per package are shown to one decimal place when not a whole number.

min_rule_weight_pt.notes: Studio print-production rule (Build Brief 01 section 7): table cell borders and outer border at no less than 0.25 pt at the exported size.

min_type_size.locator: guidance p. 6 (Legibility requirements); fact sheet p. 7
min_type_size.notes: No minimum: 'The Code does not impose additional legibility restrictions for energy statements' (guidance p. 6), and 'there are no specific size requirements for energy statements' (fact sheet p. 7). The general requirement that label text be legible, prominent and in English (Standard 1.2.1—24) still applies. If a minimum is ever set, record {"size_mm": n, "measure": "cap_height" | "x_height"}; exports below it are then blocked.
